question: What are the three parts of Canada’s Parliament?
generated_answer: The three parts of Canada’s Parliament are the Crown, the Senate, and the House of Commons. The Crown is represented by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Queen on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Senate is the upper house of Parliament, with 105 members appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister. The House of Commons is the lower house of Parliament, with 338 members elected by the people of Canada. Together, these three parts make up Canada’s bicameral parliamentary system.
